verdict.left_looks: A tall, slim tapered lighthouse with red and light-grey horizontal bands. It sits on a small cobble plinth, with a gray stone gallery and railing, a glass lantern room and a small red cap. A small brown-roofed keeper's cottage with a chimney stands beside it on a grass base with a bit of water. The tower walls are smooth and flat, with few windows and no visible door except on the cottage. The silhouette is clean and instantly reads as a lighthouse. The cottage roof stair-steps oddly at the gable end.
verdict.right_looks: A stockier tapered lighthouse with red and grey bands, built on a large mossy cobblestone and stone-brick base with stepped tiers. The tower has a wooden door, stone-brick framed windows and a lit lantern. The gallery has a fence railing, a dark brick/slate lantern room with dark-framed windows and a dark roof. An attached cottage has brick-red roof trim, timber framing, tan plaster walls and a tall cobble chimney with a lantern. The materials are varied and textured, and the details are richer. The lantern room is less distinct and looks cramped, and the cottage is partly merged into the tower base.
verdict.why: Right has more built character (a mossy stepped foundation, door, framed windows, textured materials and a timber-and-brick cottage), while Left has the cleaner lighthouse silhouette and lantern but its walls are flat and plain and its cottage roof is awkward.
